questions.stem: Which picture shows a natural material?
questions.explanation: Wood comes from trees, so it is natural. Plastic and glass are made by people.

questions.stem: Natural or made by people? Sort the pictures.
questions.explanation: Wood, stone and wool come from nature. Plastic, glass and paper are made by people.

questions.stem: Wool is a natural material.
questions.explanation: Wool comes from sheep, so it is natural.

questions.stem: Paper is found in nature. People do not make it.
questions.explanation: People make paper in factories or by hand. It is not found in nature.

questions.stem: We can ___ a sponge by pressing it hard.
questions.explanation: Pressing hard on a sponge squashes it.

questions.stem: Match each action to the thing you do it to.
questions.explanation: We squash a sponge, stretch a rubber band, twist a wet towel and bend a pipe cleaner.

questions.stem: Which one can we stretch?
questions.explanation: A balloon stretches when we blow it up. A stone and a brick do not stretch.

questions.stem: Which goes back to its shape after squashing?
questions.explanation: A sponge goes back to its shape. Clay stays in its new shape.

questions.stem: Why is a ball made of rubber, not stone?
questions.model_answer: Rubber bounces and is soft. A stone is hard and would hurt.
questions.explanation: Rubber is soft and bounces. A stone is hard and does not bounce.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to make a clay pot.
sequence: Dig clay from the river bank.
Squash and shape the clay on the wheel.
Dry the pot in the sun.
Heat the pot in a hot kiln.
questions.explanation: Mr Paul digs the clay, shapes it on the wheel, dries the pot and then heats it in the kiln.

questions.stem: Mr Paul heats clay pots in a kiln. What happens?
questions.explanation: Heating in the kiln makes the clay hard. It will never go soft again.

questions.stem: Joy wants a toy he can squash and shape. Which is best?
questions.explanation: Clay is soft and can be squashed into new shapes. Stone and glass are hard.

questions.stem: Nadia twists a wet towel to dry it. This changes its shape.
questions.explanation: Twisting changes the shape of a towel and squeezes the water out.

questions.stem: Which are made by people? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: Plastic, glass and paper are made by people. Stone and wool come from nature.

questions.stem: Match each picture to its material.
questions.explanation: A chair is made of wood, a key of metal and a bottle of plastic. Socks are made of cloth.

questions.stem: Which picture shows something made of metal?
questions.explanation: A key is made of metal. A newspaper is paper and a teddy bear is cloth.

questions.stem: A sponge stays flat after you squash it and let go.
questions.explanation: A sponge goes back to its shape. Clay is the one that stays flat.

questions.stem: Squashing, bending, twisting and ___ change the shape of materials.
questions.explanation: The four ways to change shape are squashing, bending, twisting and stretching.

questions.stem: Class 1 test: thin band 14 cm, medium 11 cm, thick 8 cm. Which stretched most?
questions.explanation: The thin band became the longest, 14 cm, so it stretched the most.

questions.stem: Thin band: 14 cm. Thick band: 8 cm. How much longer is the thin band?
questions.explanation: 14 minus 8 is 6, so the thin band was 6 cm longer.

questions.stem: Rafi squashes clay and a sponge, then lets go. What happens?

options.text: The clay stays flat. The sponge springs back.
Both go back to their shape.

questions.explanation: Clay stays squashed. A sponge goes back to its shape.

questions.stem: Sort by what happens after you squash or stretch.
questions.explanation: A sponge and a rubber band go back to their shape. Clay, play dough and a bent pipe cleaner stay in the new shape.

questions.stem: Jute is a natural material.
questions.explanation: Jute comes from plants, so it is a natural material.

questions.stem: Which picture shows something made by people?
questions.explanation: A plastic bottle is made by people in a factory. Wood and stone come from nature.
